newsitem.title: USA: Democrats protest expanded Louisiana investigation.
newsitem.headline: Democrats protest expanded Louisiana investigation.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle Friday accused Republicans of crass partisanship in their investigation of last November's Louisiana Senate election won by Democrat Mary Landrieu.

Daschle told reporters Democrats would never allow Republicans to unseat Landrieu, who defeated Republican Louis "Woody" Jenkins by 5,788 votes Nov. 5. Jenkins has alleged that Landrieu won because of fraudulent votes.

The nine Republicans on the Senate Rules Committee voted Thursday to hire an outside law firm to investigate the charges despite strong objections from the seven Democrats that Jenkins had not offered evidence to back up his claims.
Asked if he believed the Republicans were trying to steal the election, Daschle replied, "Well, that's as good a word as I can find.

"There is absolutely no possibility that Senator Landrieu will be unseated in this process," Daschle, of South Dakota, said, adding that Democrats would filibuster any attempt by Republicans to unseat her and order a new election.
Republicans have a 55-45 majority in the Senate but 60 votes are needed to end a filibuster.
"I think that what has happened (Thursday) is one of the most crass demonstrations of partisan politics that I've seen since coming to the Senate," Daschle said.

"It is extraordinarily damaging to the process, sets dangerous precedents and, in my view, has undermined our ability to work together, not only on matters pertaining to the Rules Committee, but matters that go way beyond," he said.

He also attacked Jenkins' credibility, saying, "Woody Jenkins can't take it. Woody Jenkins can't get over it. He got beat fair and square by a woman, and it's just not something he's genetically capable of accepting."

The team of lawyers was expected to go to Louisiana to interview voters and election officials but will not have power to issue subpoenas or take depositions unless the full Senate approves, and Daschle said Democrats were not likely to go along.

Jenkins has blamed New Orleans Democratic Mayor Marc Morial and his political organisation for the alleged fraud, rather than Landrieu or her campaign staff. Morial backed Landrieu, daughter of the city's former mayor, Moon Landrieu.

Separately, a three-member House panel has scheduled a hearing Saturday in Santa Ana, Calif., to investigate a challenge by former Republican Representative Bob Dornan of his defeat last November by Democrat Loretta Sanchez.
